turns.zh: 这正是我想问你的。

turns.zh: 这个点子诞生于 2024 年的 Berkshire Hathaway 年会。

turns.zh: 嗯，我当时就坐在那儿，那是 2020 年。

turns.en: there because he had passed away.

turns.en: I just had in the back of my mind this fear, like, I have a lot of Berkshire stock.
turns.zh: 我心里就一直隐隐有个担忧，就是：我手里有很多 Berkshire 的股票。

turns.en: What am I going to do with my stock when Warren Buffett passes away?
turns.zh: 等 Warren Buffett 去世以后，我该拿这些股票怎么办？

turns.en: Because I don't believe in a company the same way without him.
turns.zh: 因为如果没有了他，我对这家公司的信心就不一样了。

turns.en: Halfway through the meeting, it actually hit me that the S&P will actually be buying more
turns.zh: 年会开到一半的时候，我突然意识到，S&P 其实反而会买入更多

turns.en: Berkshire essentially on the death of Warren Buffett.
turns.zh: Berkshire——基本上就是在 Warren Buffett 去世的时候。

turns.en: I just thought, well, a lot of people don't make that connection.
turns.zh: 我就想，嗯，很多人并没有把这两件事联系起来。

turns.en: The S&P is what's called Free Float Adjusted Market Gap.
turns.zh: S&P 用的是所谓的自由流通调整市值加权（Free Float Adjusted Market Cap）。

turns.en: Berkshire might be a trillion dollars, but they're only counting the 200 billion that
turns.zh: Berkshire 也许值一万亿美元，但指数只会计入其中一部分，

turns.en: he owns, or 20% that he owns, is not counted.
turns.zh: 他所持有的那 2000 亿美元、也就是 20% 的股份，是不被计入的。

turns.en: When he dies, those shares will become free floating.
turns.zh: 等他去世以后，那些股份就会变成自由流通股（free floating）。

turns.en: I just thought, well, why would anybody want more exposure to Berkshire absent Warren Buffett?
turns.zh: 我就想，嗯，如果没有了 Warren Buffett，为什么还会有人想要更多地持有 Berkshire 呢？

turns.en: In the same respect, who would want more exposure to Tesla without Elon Musk or Metta without
turns.zh: 同样的道理，谁会在没有 Elon Musk 的情况下更想持有 Tesla，或者在没有

turns.en: Mark Zuckerberg?
turns.zh: Mark Zuckerberg 的情况下更想持有 Meta 呢？

turns.en: These guys are super geniuses.
turns.zh: 这些人都是绝顶天才。

turns.en: We should want more exposure to these companies while they're there and their ownership is
turns.zh: 我们应该在他们还在、他们的持股也

turns.en: there and less so when they're gone.
turns.zh: 还在的时候更多地持有这些公司，而在他们离开之后少持有。

turns.en: I came home from Omaha and just had to find all this ownership data.
turns.zh: 我从 Omaha 回到家后，就一门心思想把这些持股数据都找出来。

turns.en: I looked at Bloomberg, CapIQ, FACTSET, all the data providers, and surprisingly, nobody
turns.zh: 我查了 Bloomberg、CapIQ、FACTSET，所有这些数据供应商，结果出乎意料，居然没有

turns.en: actually had the ownership data going back that far.
turns.zh: 一家真正拥有能追溯到那么久远的持股数据。

turns.en: I had to manually go through every proxy filing and collect the data myself.
turns.zh: 我只能手动翻阅每一份代理权声明文件（proxy filing），自己把数据收集起来。

turns.en: I went back 20 years to launch the index, but I went back 100 years to see what would
turns.zh: 为了推出这个指数，我往前追溯了 20 年，但为了看看如果你当初投资

turns.en: it look like had you invested.
turns.zh: 会是什么结果，我往前追溯了 100 年。

turns.en: For 100 years, you could see that the best-performing companies had leadership at the top that was
turns.zh: 在这 100 年里，你能看到，那些表现最好的公司，其最高领导层都是

turns.en: responsible.
turns.zh: 负责任的。

turns.en: Once those leaders were gone, the companies typically went through a decay.
turns.zh: 而一旦这些领导者离开，公司通常就会走向衰败。

turns.en: I went back 100 years, looked at the number one company in the world, and 1930-1950 was
turns.zh: 我往前追溯 100 年，看了每个阶段全球排名第一的公司，1930 到 1950 年间是

turns.en: General Motors and it was one man, Alfred Sloan, responsible.
turns.zh: General Motors，而掌舵的就是一个人——Alfred Sloan。

turns.en: IBM was the biggest company in the world in the 70s and 80s.
turns.zh: IBM 在七八十年代是全球最大的公司。

turns.en: Again, there's one guy responsible for that.
turns.zh: 同样，也是由一个人负责的。

turns.en: It was Thomas Watson Jr., the son of the founder.
turns.zh: 那就是 Thomas Watson Jr.，创始人的儿子。

turns.en: He was the chairman of the board for most of that time.
turns.zh: 在那段时间里，他大部分时候都担任董事长（chairman of the board）。

turns.en: Jack Welch with GE.
turns.zh: GE 有 Jack Welch。

turns.en: The only exception I can really find is Apple has continued to do well despite Steve Jobs
turns.zh: 我真正能找到的唯一例外是 Apple，尽管 Steve Jobs

turns.en: not being around.
turns.zh: 已经不在了，它依然表现得很好。

turns.en: There's exceptions, but for the most part, the index has a basket of stocks run by owners.
turns.zh: 例外是有的，但总的来说，这个指数装的是由所有者亲自经营的一篮子股票。

turns.en: Interesting.
turns.zh: 有意思。

turns.en: Well, we're going to get into the fun and the strategy here in a minute.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们待会儿就会深入聊聊这只基金和它的策略。

turns.en: Before we do that, though, I always like to ask every guest, what do you like to do when

turns.en: you're not working?
turns.zh: 工作的时候，你喜欢做些什么？

turns.zh: 有什么爱好吗？

turns.en: I play a little bit of beach volleyball for exercise, and I read a lot.
turns.zh: 我会打打沙滩排球锻炼身体，也读很多书。

turns.en: I go out to dinner, enjoy nice dinners.
turns.zh: 我会出去吃吃饭，享受美食。

turns.en: Love that.
turns.zh: 真不错。

turns.en: Let's get into OWN, which is the ETF behind the, or I should say in front of this index.
turns.zh: 我们来聊聊 OWN，它是这个指数背后的——或者说我该说是这个指数前面的那只 ETF。

turns.en: The index is behind it, which is the inside ownership 100 ETF.
turns.zh: 指数在它背后，它就是 Inside Ownership 100 ETF。

turns.en: This was launched on June 3rd at a high level.
turns.zh: 这只 ETF 是在 6 月 3 日推出的。从大的方面来说，

turns.en: We touched on it, but really at a high level, what is this fun and what is the core problem
turns.zh: 我们刚才提到了它，但真正从大的方面讲，这只基金是什么？它要解决的

turns.en: that it's solving?
turns.zh: 核心问题又是什么？

turns.en: Well, I like to tell people there's three ways you could index.
turns.zh: 嗯，我喜欢跟人说，做指数有三种方式。

turns.en: The first is equal weighted.
turns.zh: 第一种是等权重（equal weighted）。

turns.en: You could buy S&P 500 equal weighted and you systematically buy every single company equally
turns.zh: 你可以买入 S&P 500 等权重版本，系统性地对每一家公司都等额

turns.en: and every quarter you trim, the ones that go up and you feed the ones that go down.
turns.zh: 买入，然后每个季度你会减持那些上涨的、加仓那些下跌的。

turns.en: It's systematic by low sell high, right?
turns.zh: 这就是系统性的高抛低吸，对吧？

turns.en: Or you recognize that there's going to be some extreme winners and they're going to
turns.zh: 或者你认识到，会有一些极端的赢家出现，它们将会

turns.en: compound your earnings for a very long time and you want to increase your exposure as
turns.zh: 在很长时间里让你的收益不断复利增长，你想随着

turns.en: those companies grow.
turns.zh: 这些公司的成长而增加你的持仓。

turns.en: You mark a cap weight or you recognize that there's going to be a handful of individuals
turns.zh: 你就用市值加权（market cap weight）；或者你认识到，会有少数几个人

turns.en: that really change the world, but you don't know which ones.
turns.zh: 真正改变世界，但你不知道是哪几个。

turns.en: Rather than index to market cap, you index to the individuals behind the corporation,
turns.zh: 与其按市值来做指数，不如按公司背后的那些人来做指数，

turns.en: the owners.
turns.zh: 也就是所有者。

turns.en: Again, you don't know which ones are going to really tick off, but you index to them.
turns.zh: 同样，你不知道哪些人最终会真正一鸣惊人，但你就按他们来做指数。

turns.en: What you get is a handful of exceptional leaders that really hit the ball in the park, like
turns.zh: 你得到的就是少数几位真正打出全垒打的杰出领导者，比如

turns.en: Jensen, Elon Musk, Warren Buffett, Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos.
turns.zh: Jensen、Elon Musk、Warren Buffett、Mark Zuckerberg、Jeff Bezos。

turns.en: By indexing to these leaders, it's more power law driven, so you're getting more exposure
turns.zh: 通过按这些领导者来做指数，它更多是由幂律（power law）驱动的，所以你会更多地持有

turns.en: to these extraordinary companies, extraordinary leaders.
turns.zh: 这些非凡的公司、非凡的领导者。

turns.en: The core argument that you made earlier, and I just want to touch on it again because for
turns.zh: 你刚才提出的那个核心论点，我想再谈一下，因为对于

turns.en: the advisors listening to this show, I think it's important, the core argument is how the
turns.zh: 在听这档节目的投资顾问来说，我觉得这一点很重要——这个核心论点讲的是

turns.en: S&P is actually built.
turns.zh: S&P 实际上是如何构建的。

turns.en: Because it's free float adjusted, which means shares held by founders and controlling insiders
turns.zh: 因为它是自由流通调整的（free float adjusted），这意味着创始人和控股内部人持有的股份

turns.en: get excluded, so walk us through why that matters in practice.
turns.zh: 会被剔除出去，那你来给我们讲讲，为什么这在实践中很重要。

turns.en: Think about it.
turns.zh: 你想一想。

turns.en: The best investors in the world are actually not investors at all, they're entrepreneurs
turns.zh: 世界上最好的投资者其实根本不是投资者，而是那些

turns.en: who never sold.
turns.zh: 从未卖出过的创业者。

turns.en: Why would you want to exclude shares that are held by the best investors or the best value
turns.zh: 你为什么要去剔除那些由世界上最好的投资者、最好的价值

turns.en: creators in the world?
turns.zh: 创造者所持有的股份呢？

turns.en: It makes no sense.
turns.zh: 这毫无道理。

turns.en: You should want to have more exposure to these companies while these leaders are there.
turns.zh: 你应该希望在这些领导者还在的时候，更多地持有这些公司。

turns.en: So think, you have two companies, A and B.
turns.zh: 那么设想一下，你有两家公司，A 和 B。

turns.en: A, let's call them identical.
turns.zh: 我们姑且称它们完全一样。

turns.en: Identical companies are doing identical things and identical size.
turns.zh: 两家完全一样的公司，做着完全一样的事，规模也完全一样。

turns.en: But company B has a CEO who owns 20% of the company.
turns.zh: 但 B 公司的 CEO 持有公司 20% 的股份。

turns.en: Company A is run by a boardroom, with a CEO, a hired CEO, and a boardroom with really owns
turns.zh: 而 A 公司是由董事会管理的，有一个 CEO，一个受雇的 CEO，还有一个几乎不持

turns.en: no stock.
turns.zh: 股的董事会。

turns.en: The S&P will give you more exposure to company A, when probably company B is the one that
turns.zh: S&P 会让你更多地持有 A 公司，可实际上 B 公司才更可能是那个

turns.en: you want to maximize exposure to.
turns.zh: 你最想加大持仓的公司。

turns.en: The actual example I have for that is Intel and Nvidia.
turns.zh: 我这方面一个真实的例子就是 Intel 和 Nvidia。

turns.en: In July of 2020, Intel and Nvidia were identical companies.
turns.zh: 在 2020 年 7 月，Intel 和 Nvidia 还是体量相当的公司。

turns.en: They're both $250 billion companies, almost the same weighting in the S&P, around 1%.
turns.zh: 它们都是 2500 亿美元市值的公司，在 S&P 里的权重也几乎相同，大约都是 1%。

turns.en: Intel had seven times the revenue of Nvidia at that moment.
turns.zh: 在那个时点，Intel 的营收是 Nvidia 的七倍。

turns.en: Seven times the profits, a higher return on equity, and a higher free cash flow yield.
turns.zh: 利润是它的七倍，还有更高的净资产收益率（return on equity）和更高的自由现金流收益率（free cash flow yield）。

turns.en: But Nvidia had something Intel didn't.
turns.zh: 但 Nvidia 有一样 Intel 没有的东西。

turns.en: They had a CEO, a founder CEO with extreme ownership, who went to bed thinking about
turns.zh: 他们有一位 CEO，一位持股比例极高的创始人 CEO，他睡觉时想的

turns.en: the company, woke up thinking about it.
turns.zh: 是公司，醒来时想的还是公司。

turns.en: And fast forward six years, Nvidia has created enormous wealth for shareholders of more than
turns.zh: 而快进六年之后，Nvidia 为股东创造了超过
2000% 的巨大财富。

turns.en: And Intel has underperformed the market.
turns.zh: 而 Intel 则跑输了大盘。

turns.en: So I think investors have paid too little attention to how much the CEO and the board
turns.zh: 所以我认为，投资者对 CEO 和董事会

turns.en: own and what they're capable of, and probably too much attention to last year's earnings.
turns.zh: 持有多少股、他们有多大本事，关注得太少，而去年的盈利，可能关注得太多了。

turns.en: And more and more, I think, studying the last year's earnings is going to be less predictive
turns.zh: 而且我觉得，越来越明显的是，研究去年的盈利对未来盈利的

turns.en: of what future earnings are going to look like, especially with AI.
turns.zh: 预测性会越来越弱，尤其是在 AI 时代。

turns.en: The world is changing too fast, and using last year's earnings or earnings five years
turns.zh: 这个世界变化太快了，用去年的盈利或者五年前的盈利，

turns.en: ago is not going to tell you much about what earnings are going to look like five years
turns.zh: 并不能告诉你多少关于五年后盈利会是什么样子

turns.en: from now.
turns.zh: 的信息。

turns.en: So walk us through the methodology a little bit.
turns.zh: 那你来给我们讲讲这个方法论（methodology）吧。

turns.en: You start with the S&P 500 as the entire universe, and then pick the top 100 by dollar
turns.zh: 你先以整个 S&P 500 作为全部的股票池，然后按内部人持股的

turns.en: value of insider ownership, and then you wait by insider stake instead of market cap.
turns.zh: 美元价值挑出前 100 名，再按内部人持股、而不是市值来加权（weight）。

turns.en: So why dollar value rather than percentage?
turns.zh: 那为什么用美元价值，而不是百分比呢？

turns.en: Well, we want to be somewhat like market cap.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们希望在某种程度上接近市值加权。

turns.en: So essentially, we're counting the market cap of each company by only the shares held
turns.zh: 所以本质上，我们在计算每家公司的市值时，只算内部人

turns.en: by insiders rather than all the shares outstanding.
